series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Across 119 symbols with ≥4y D1 history, fit Ridge on OHLC to forecast 10-day close return vs a null that always predicts the mean (inputs forced to 0). Score = RSS/TSS from 5-fold TimeSeriesSplit(gap=HORIZON); markets with score<1 (~8%) are flagged as having learnable inefficiency vs mean-hugging.
data_needed: D1 OHLC ≥4 years per symbol; 10-day forward return target; TimeSeriesSplit CV
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: 119 broker symbols filtered from 333; EURUSD deep-dive; D1; HORIZON=10
why_new_for_mis: Turns classical R²-style RSS/TSS into a cross-sectional sensing screen that ranks instruments by how much they beat a mean-forecast null—usable as an instrument-selection sensor before any regime model.
quote: over 4 years, we could not outperform a model always predicting the average return for about 91.6% of all the markets we tested

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Train two independent RandomForest models on identical OHLC+delta+SMA5 features: one predicts Trend Profit (SMA-cross trend actions × 10d return), the other Mean Reverting Profit (inverted actions × return). Out-of-sample, require pred_trend+pred_mean≈0 (L2 norm 0) as an EMH consistency gate; trade only the model with positive expected profit—dynamically switching regime without a separate HMM.
data_needed: EURUSD D1 OHLC, SMA(5), 10-day returns; dual strategy-profit labels; ONNX dual models
why_new_for_mis: Regime sensor is the argmax of two opposing strategy-profit forecasts gated by sum-to-zero EMH check, not a latent-state classifier on price alone.
quote: If the maximum value of the sum of the model's predictions equals 0.0, then our model has passed our test... our strategy, has the ability to change strategy without human intervention

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Pull identical 4y D1 EURUSD from two brokers; compare mean/variance of 10-day returns, max drawdown of returns, tick_volume trends, Pearson corr of OHLC (~0.41), and RSS/TSS forecastability. Treat broker-pair divergence (return sign flips, 21% risk gap, 7% forecastability gap) as a feed-quality / liquidity-structure sensor rather than assuming one true EURUSD.
data_needed: Parallel OHLC+tick_volume+spread from ≥2 brokers; aligned row counts; 10-day return labels
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; D1; 1460 rows (~4y); HORIZON=10; Broker A vs B
why_new_for_mis: Senses market microstructure via broker-feed disagreement (correlation, tick-volume shape, return moments) instead of treating venue quotes as interchangeable.
quote: the EURUSD market moves in different directions across different brokers... correlation levels of only 0.41

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Online linear model (pseudo-inverse) on rolling snapshots of OHLC, equity/balance, EMA high/low, account-state one-hots. Predicts account balance at next candle and at +HORIZON(10); grant trade permission only if prediction[4]<prediction[8] (positive expected balance slope). Avoids comparing model output to live price (manifold misalignment / geometric irreducible error).
data_needed: D1 OHLC, EMA(10) high/low, ATR(14), account balance/equity, 90+ observation buffer
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; PERIOD_D1; HORIZON=10; MA_PERIOD=10; backtest 2020-01 to 2025-05
why_new_for_mis: Regime/permission sensor is the sign of multi-horizon predicted equity slope in model-coordinate space, not predicted price vs spot.
quote: we traded the slope predicted by the model over two intervals, rather than making a direct comparison of predicted and actual prices

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Single multi-output LinearRegression/ONNX predicts MA-close/high/low at horizons H={1,5,10}. Trade signal is slope between model predictions at short vs long horizon (e.g. pred_MA_H[1] vs pred_MA_H[10]), optionally on midpoint ((MA_H+MA_L)/2) growth—never pred vs live close. Combined with M15 breakout gate and ATR trailing on D1.
data_needed: D1 OHLC + SMA(5) OHLC + 5-step diffs; 9 multi-horizon MA targets; ONNX multi-output
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; TF_1=D1 features, TF_2=M15 entries; H1=1,H2=5,H3=10; backtest Mar 2022–May 2025
why_new_for_mis: Change/regime-direction sensor is intra-prediction slope across forecast horizons, staying in one manifold to sidestep geometric irreducible error.
quote: our model's predictions may be more profitable for us when compared against themselves than when compared against the real target

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: On a short ~2y EURUSD D1 window, difference OHLC as inputs and use TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=5,gap=HORIZON) inside RandomizedSearchCV to tune MLPRegressor (activation/alpha/layers/solver/lr). Gap equals forecast horizon to block leakage; selected NN then ONNX-exported for D1 trade signals vs Ridge baseline.
data_needed: EURUSD D1 OHLC diffs; HORIZON=1 target; RandomizedSearchCV+TimeSeriesSplit
why_new_for_mis: Packages horizon-gapped TSCV as the validation sensor that makes small-sample neural sequence models trustworthy for MIS neural_sensor pipelines.
quote: time series data cannot be shuffled, as that would leak future information into the past

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Effective Memory Cross-Validation: fix a ~4y test set; train identical models on most-recent fractions {10%…100%} of an ~4y train set (≈8y EURUSD D1 total). Plot OOS RMSE vs fraction; minimum at ~80% means oldest ~1y is harmful (information decay). Deploy model trained only on the effective-memory window, optionally with longer forecast horizon.
data_needed: Long D1 OHLC history; expanding most-recent train partitions; fixed holdout test RMSE
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; D1; ~3000 bars; classical HORIZON=1 baseline vs improved HORIZON=10 on 80% partition
why_new_for_mis: Senses the market’s effective memory length—a data-relevance / regime-stability horizon—rather than assuming more history always helps.
quote: the lowest out-of-sample error occurred from the model that was fit using only 80% of the available training data, not all of it

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Estimate cumulative returns of MA-OC, MA-HL, RSI>50, Stochastic bands strategies on EURUSD. SVD on the strategy-return matrix; take first k singular values covering ≥80% variance; read VT loadings—strategies with positive loading on dominant modes form risk-tiered portfolios (High/Mid/Low/Minimum). Live EA votes only among positively loaded strategies for the selected mode.
data_needed: OHLC + SMA OHLC + RSI(15) + Stochastic; strategy signed returns × HORIZON=5 market return; SVD U,S,VT
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; PERIOD_CURRENT (D1 in practice); MA=5; RSI=15; Stoch 5/3/3; HORIZON=5
why_new_for_mis: Regime modes are principal components of a strategy-PnL matrix, yielding which indicator rules are currently favored—white-box regime sensing without price HMM.
quote: Each mode of variation reflects a distinct behavioral pattern the market can adopt

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: MLPRegressor (RandomizedSearchCV+TimeSeriesSplit) maps OHLC+MA+RSI+Stoch features to multi-horizon cumulative strategy-return targets. At runtime, compute per-strategy predicted slope (target_t+H − target_t+1); if max slope>0, execute the ArgMax strategy’s rule—black-box automatic strategy selection conditioned on current market state.
data_needed: Same indicator panel as SVD path; multi-output strategy return horizons; ONNX MLP
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; 11 ONNX inputs (OHLC, MA O/H/L/C, RSI, Stoch main/signal); 8 outputs; daily bars
why_new_for_mis: Neural sequence sensor outputs which elementary strategy is expected to earn next, enabling MIS to switch sensing/trading modes from market features alone.
quote: check whether the slope of the cumulative balance is positive. If so, we place trades aligned with the strategy that exhibits the largest expected slope

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: From OHLC alone, synthesize midpoint targets (O-H, O-L, O-C, H-L, H-C, L-C). Binary-classify up/down of each at HORIZON=2 with LDA under TimeSeriesSplit; pick the easiest target (O-H mid ~70.8% vs classical Close ~50.3%). Verify surrogate tracks Close via LinearRegression coef≈0.995 / correlation, then RandomForest-regress the midpoint level for D1 signals vs current O-H mid.
data_needed: OHLC + arithmetic midpoints; binary and level labels at HORIZON; CV accuracy ranking; optional FastICA check
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; PERIOD_CURRENT/D1; HORIZON=2; 5y backtest Feb 2020–2025; ATR(14) stops
why_new_for_mis: Self-supervised sensing: generate and rank surrogate targets that are guaranteed functions of observations, then trade the learnable midpoint that still tracks price.
quote: By designing your own targets from the observations you started with, you can attain new error levels you would never attain if you bound yourself to the classical fixed target of future price
